title: Could Mobile AI be Exploited?: Understanding the Exploitations of Trust and Ethics Gap in On-Device Small Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2406.05364v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: In this paper, we present a very first study to investigate trust and ethical implications of on-device artificial intelligence (AI), focusing on small language models (SLMs) amenable for personal devices like smartphones. While on-device SLMs promise enhanced privacy, reduced latency, and improved user experience compared to cloud-based services, we posit that they might also introduce significant risks and vulnerabilities compared to their on-server counterparts. As part of our study, we conduct a systematic evaluation of the state-of-the-art on-devices SLMs, compared to their on-server counterparts, using well-established trust and ethics frameworks. Our results illustrate that on-device SLMs are significantly less trustworthy and lacks ethical safeguards, specifically demonstrating more stereotypical, unfair, privacy-breaching and harmful content generation behavior. Further, these risks of on-device SLMs could be exploited

translated_title: 移动AI会被利用吗？：理解设备端小型语言模型中信任与伦理差距的被利用问题
translated_abstract: 在本文中，我们提出了首个研究来调查设备端人工智能（AI）的信任与伦理影响，重点关注适用于智能手机等个人设备的小型语言模型（SLM）。虽然与基于云端的服务相比，设备端SLM有望提供更强的隐私保护、更低的延迟和更好的用户体验，但我们认为，与服务器端对应模型相比，它们也可能引入重大风险和漏洞。作为研究的一部分，我们使用成熟的信任与伦理框架，对最先进的设备端SLM与服务器端对应模型进行了系统性评估。我们的结果表明，设备端SLM的可信度显著较低且缺乏伦理保障，具体表现为生成更多刻板印象、不公平、侵犯隐私和有害内容的行为。此外，设备端SLM的这些风险可能被恶意利用
tldr: 本文首次系统评估了设备端小型语言模型，发现其相比服务器端模型可信度和伦理保障显著不足，更易生成刻板印象、不公平、侵犯隐私及有害内容，且这些风险可能被恶意利用。
en_tdlr: This paper presents the first systematic evaluation revealing that on-device small language models are significantly less trustworthy and lack ethical safeguards compared to server-based counterparts, exhibiting more stereotypical, unfair, privacy-breaching, and harmful content generation that could be exploited.
